sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A rhizomatous perennial, 15–50 cm tall, native across much of temperate Eurasia. It grows at woodland edges and in warm, dry scrub. Deeply divided basal leaves accompany a solitary flower about 4–7 cm across, usually with five or six white petal-like sepals but no true petals. The separate carpels mature into hairy achenes.

sections.title: Toxicity and distinction
sections.text: USDA GRIN records a poison use for mammals but provides no details about human exposure; this does not support a general human toxicity claim. The species is distinct from Anemone nemorosa, also commonly called wood anemone.
